record.original_question: Study the ELMS conjecture on exceptional curves, in the setting described in the source.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{X}$ be an exceptional curve in the sense of Lenzing–Kussin, i.e. a noncommutative smooth projective curve of genus zero over a field $k$: a small connected hereditary $k$-linear abelian category $\mathcal{H} = \mathrm{coh}(\mathbb{X})$ that contains a tilting object, that has Serre duality, and whose objects decompose into a "line bundle" part and a torsion part formed of tubes. Equivalently, $\mathbb{X}$ is a weighted noncommutative regular projective curve over $k$, obtained from a noncommutative regular projective curve of genus zero by attaching positive integer weights at finitely many closed points.

The "ELMS conjecture" on exceptional curves asserts a precise structural prediction about $\mathbb{X}$ (for instance, on the classification, function field invariants, or representation-theoretic invariants of exceptional curves of a given type). Resolve this conjecture: either prove that the predicted statement holds for every exceptional curve $\mathbb{X}$ over an arbitrary base field $k$, or exhibit an exceptional curve violating it.
artifact.category_tag: Exceptional curves and weighted projective lines
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for the "ELMS conjecture" in the context of exceptional curves did not return a definitive identification of the statement or a resolution. Related work on exceptional/weighted noncommutative regular projective curves (Kussin, Lenzing, and collaborators) continues to appear (e.g. classifications of tubular and elliptic exceptional curves, cotilting and large tilting sheaves, exceptional hereditary curves and real curve orbifolds), but no source consulted records the ELMS conjecture as proved or refuted. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Weighted noncommutative regular projective curves (Kussin)
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies noncommutative 2-orbifolds of nonnegative Euler characteristic — real elliptic, domestic and tubular exceptional curves.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational framework for exceptional curves; no resolution of an 'ELMS conjecture' stated.

status_evidence.title: Exceptional hereditary curves and real curve orbifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Develops theory of exceptional hereditary curves over arbitrary fields via equivariant coherent sheaves on regular projective curves of genus zero.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on exceptional curves continues; the ELMS conjecture is not recorded as solved here.

status_evidence.title: Non-crossing partitions for exceptional hereditary curves
status_evidence.snippet: Studies thick subcategory posets for exceptional hereditary curves.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on exceptional curves in 2025 without indicating that the ELMS conjecture has been settled.
